summary: Master the essentials of Open Market Operations and Liquidity Management. Join our training to boost your expertise and navigate financial markets effectively.
lede: Open market operations and liquidity management involve forecasting and managing reserves through money market operations and liquidity frameworks. For professionals in monetary operations, liquidity risk and treasury, the course develops practical skills in liquidity forecasting, repo and reverse repo auction design, corridor and standing facility structuring, and intraday or stress-liquidity planning.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for professionals who already work with monetary policy operations, liquidity decisions, and money market activities, and who need to deepen their practical command of open market tools and liquidity management frameworks.
audience: Treasury Manager in a commercial bank
modules: Monetary Policy Implementation and Money Market Foundations
Liquidity Management Frameworks and Interest Rate Corridors
Liquidity Forecasting Models and Data-Driven Tools
Design and Execution of Open Market Operations
Basel III Liquidity Metrics and Market Impact
Intraday Liquidity and Treasury Market Operations
Stress Liquidity Management and Crisis OMOs
Integration, Governance, and Reporting for Liquidity Operations
prerequisites: This is an intermediate to advanced course. You should have working knowledge of basic monetary economics, money market instruments, and bank balance sheets, plus at least 2–3 years of experience in central banking, treasury, ALM, liquidity risk, or related financial markets roles. You should understand core concepts such as policy rates, yield curves, repos, and reserve requirements. No programming is required. Spreadsheet literacy (e.g., Excel or similar) is essential because you will work through liquidity forecasts, simple LCR-style metrics, and OMO allocation examples using provided templates. Advanced topics such as unconventional monetary policy, CBDC implications, and automated liquidity dashboards are taught at conceptual and operational application level, not full technical engineering depth.
